title: Industrial dispute reference - the process before the labour court
p1:
A labour dispute does not reach the courtroom the moment an employee and employer disagree.

Many people assume a worker can directly file a case before the Labour Court. The reality is that there is a process before the court even begins examining the dispute.
p2: The surprising part is that the Labour Court usually gets involved only after the dispute is formally referred by the appropriate government authority. This reference acts as the gateway that gives the court power to decide the matter.
p3:
Before the reference, the dispute may go through discussions, conciliation, and efforts by labour authorities to find a settlement. If those efforts fail, the matter can be referred to the Labour Court for adjudication.

The practical takeaway: the reference stage is not just paperwork. It decides whether a labour dispute moves from negotiation to legal determination.
conclusion: Did you know that a Labour Court generally cannot start deciding an industrial dispute unless it receives a formal reference? What are your views on this process?
